findings.reason: without the host-presence test the builder either drops the per-session branch or guesses at it, and a hostless pane with two followers (a Monitor follower overlapping its 29-minute re-arm) draws each lift transition twice, the exact duplication §51 exists to stop.
findings.text: §51's Deliverable says the lift claim is "keyed on the host that spawned them, the RECKON_FOLLOWER_OWNER pair SessionHost._spawn stamps on each child and follower_owner() in reckon/crew/follower_registration.py reads back", and two sentences later says "A follower with no host keeps the per-session key". `follower_owner()` cannot distinguish the two cases: `_FollowerOwnerCache.resolve` reads `RECKON_FOLLOWER_OWNER` and, when it is absent, falls back to `os.getppid()` (reckon/crew/follower_registration.py:465-490), so it returns a `(pid, start)` pair for a host-armed follower and for a hostless one alike; the presence of the host's stamp is never surfaced. A builder who keys the claim on `follower_owner()` unconditionally therefore gives a hostless follower a ppid-derived key rather than the session key the Deliverable declares, and the gate cannot catch it, because its hostless case runs a single follower and draws once under either key. The mechanism needs the host-presence signal named — the presence of `RECKON_FOLLOWER_OWNER` itself, or of the host's `RECKON_SESSION_HOST_SETTLE` (reckon/crew/session_host.py:442) — since otherwise the declared hostless behaviour is unimplementable from the mechanism as written.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `lift_claim_dir` (reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:1126), `RECKON_FOLLOWER_OWNER`/`_spawn` (reckon/crew/session_host.py:425,435) and `follower_owner` (reckon/crew/follower_registration.py:501) all exist and read as the section describes; §23 and §49 are real sections.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — the gate is falsifiable: one host over two sessions must draw one grant and one end row, and the negative control re-keys the claim on the session and must then draw two rows, which is red at base.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the gate log is written under the run directory; the write paths are the two repository source/test files, not a scratch or node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the test file and the described symbols name the mechanism (`test_a_pane_draws_a_lift_once_per_host`), with no plan label, stage name or ticket number.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the deliverable names `follower_owner()` as the reader of the host key while also requiring a hostless follower to keep the per-session key, but `follower_owner()` returns a value whether or not a host stamped one, so it cannot make that distinction.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one deliverable, the host-keyed lift claim; the release-request half an earlier review flagged has been removed from the section.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §51's ordering behind §50 is carried by a real edge in `plan-section-depends-on` (`s51: ["the-monitor-shows-the-work-it-watches#s50"]`) and by the open followup `f-tmstwiw-051`, not by prose alone.
